\section{Games}\label{sec:games}

\begin{figure*}[t]
\begin{minipage}{.48\textwidth}
\begin{algorithmic}[1]
\Statex \underline{$\G{0}$}
\State $x\sample\{0,1\}^n$
\If{$x = 0$}
  \State \Return $1$ \Comment{a comment with 50\% percent}
\EndIf
\end{algorithmic}
\end{minipage}\hfill
\begin{minipage}{.48\textwidth}
\begin{algorithmic}[1]
\Statex \underline{$\G{1}$}
\For{$i=1,\dots,\qq$}
  \State $y_i\sample\{0,1\}^n$
\EndFor
\end{algorithmic}
\end{minipage}
\caption{Games $\G{0}$ and $\G{1}$, side by side, across both columns.}\label{fig:games}
\end{figure*}

\begin{definition}[Imaginary oracle]\label{def:oracle}
An oracle is \emph{imaginary} if it answers $\bot$ on every query $x\in\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[First]\label{lem:one}
$\Pr[\G{0}^{\Adv}=1]\le\Pr[\G{1}^{\Adv}=1]+\negl(n)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
By \cref{def:oracle}, the games are identical until bad, so
\begin{align}
  \Pr[\G{0}^{\Adv}=1] &\le \Pr[\G{1}^{\Adv}=1] + \Pr[\mathsf{bad}] \label{eq:hop}\\
  &\le \Pr[\G{1}^{\Adv}=1] + \frac{\qq^2}{2^n}. \label{eq:bound}
\end{align}
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:two}
Every query costs at most one unit.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lstlisting}
proc main() = {
  var x : int;      (* 50% of the time; a $dollar *)
  x <- 3%r;
  return x;
}
\end{lstlisting}
